name: asked-and-answered
sub: They said someone had emptied it — the earliest answer
on record, written in Matthew's own Gospel. (Matthew 28:13)
thread:
You are not the first person to ask.

The hardest question you have about the Christian faith is almost certainly older than you think.

Here is the earliest response Jesus' opponents left on record — and where it is written down. 🧵

Open Matthew 28. The charge is right there in the text:

"His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep." (Matthew 28:13)

Read it again. His opponents did not say the grave was full. They said someone had emptied it.

Matthew did not bury the charge.

He wrote it down — inside his own Gospel, and noted that the charge was still being told: "This story has been spread among the Jews to this day." (Matthew 28:15, ESV)

Around AD 150, Justin Martyr records the same charge — still being spread, generations later (Dialogue with Trypho 108).

He records it inside a long, public dialogue with a Jewish teacher, preserving the objection rather than omitting it.

Around AD 248, Origen answers the philosopher Celsus — who had written some seventy years earlier — point by point, across eight books.

He quotes Celsus so fully that most of Celsus' own work survives only inside the reply that answers it.

Twenty centuries, and the pattern never changes. Every generation brings its hardest question; in every generation someone answers it in writing.

Recording an objection is not the same as answering it well. Both are on the record. Read them and judge.

That charge was never hidden. It is printed in Matthew's own Gospel.

That is what Asked & Answered does.

Paste the tweet. Paste the screenshot. Or just ask in your own words. You get a clear answer in plain language — and when the objection has a name on it, the person who pressed it, often centuries before you saw it.

You are not the first to ask.
